iconicAnchor.label: DEC VT100 terminal
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: The VT100 is a widely emulated 1978 video terminal whose text display, fixed character system, bold and alternate character capabilities, and dedicated hardware define the historical command-screen substrate.

sources.title: VT100 terminal
supports: DEC introduced the VT100 in 1978 as a dedicated text terminal.
Its display supported bold characters and multiple text and graphic character sets, reinforcing a strict character-cell interface rather than a modern code editor.

sources.title: TeleVideo 803 Microcomputer
sources.publisher: Smithsonian National Museum of American History
supports: The TeleVideo 803 used a large tilting green display in an integrated early-1980s computer system.
The museum identifies the VT100 as the reference terminal model copied by competing manufacturers, supporting its canonical role.
